findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the concrete transcript-capture seam in step 2 (e.g. monkeypatch `rebar.llm.pai_tools.filesystem_tools` to return argument-logging wrappers, or post-hoc reduce the run's pydantic-ai message history like `usage_log` does) and state that it captures full arguments for ALL three FS tools (read_file, search_files, list_directory) plus show_ticket.
evidence: Plan quote: 'wrap the verifier's tool executor in-harness (monkeypatch at the workflow seam) to log every tool call with full arguments'
Contrast: step 1 pins completion_verdict_cache.py:59, step 3 pins completion.py:237 + completion_banking.py:38, step 5 pins gate_ops.py:48/:229 — step 2 pins nothing
'Why' names this the blocker: 'verifier telemetry does not carry argument-level tool-call transcripts — the PoC must capture them harness-side'

Feasibility CONFIRMED (not a capability gap): tools are plain closures from filesystem_tools(repo_path) at src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py:67-73 bound into a pydantic-ai Agent; a run-shape reducer already reconstructs tool-call args from message history (docs/llm-framework.md:478-484). Evidence class: Partially-verified — the integration point exists, the specific surface the plan intends is unconfirmed.
findings.finding: Step 2's transcript-capture seam — the capability the 'Why' section names as the design-time BLOCKER — is asserted but not pinned to a concrete symbol, unlike every other step which cites an exact file:line monkeypatch target.
scenarios: Harness author cannot locate the intended wrap point and picks an ad-hoc seam that misses some tool calls (e.g. wraps read_file but not search_files/list_directory), corrupting the overlap-rate metric
The chosen seam captures tool NAMES but not full arguments (paths/patterns), which the frontier extraction in step 4 strictly requires
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the seam to `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py:filesystem_tools` (wrap each returned closure to record name+args) or to the run's message history via the existing run-shape reducer, and enumerate the tools whose arguments must be logged so frontier extraction (step 4) has a complete searched-set.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the fallback when forced-exhaustion attempt 1 does NOT fail insufficiency-only (clean PASS, genuine criterion FAIL, or provider error): e.g. lower the budget and retry, drop the ticket from the corpus, or record INDETERMINATE — and say how the seed cache/frontier is handled in each case.
evidence: Plan quote: 'attempt 1 then FAILs insufficiency-only with a partial bank; keep the transcript.'
The reduced budget is only a floor override; nothing forces the verifier to run out of steps rather than PASS or hit a real FAIL within 12-20 steps.

ABSENCE: no branch describing what the harness does if attempt 1 does not fail insufficiency-only (retry with a lower budget? discard the ticket? mark INDETERMINATE?), yet its transcript+bank are the seed for both arms.
findings.finding: The protocol asserts forced-exhaustion attempt 1 'FAILs insufficiency-only with a partial bank' as a guaranteed outcome, but a reduced budget (12-20 steps) can instead produce a clean PASS, a genuine (non-insufficiency) criterion FAIL, or a provider/environmental error; no fallback is specified for these outcomes, and attempt 1 seeds the cache copy and frontier for every downstream arm.
findings.location: Protocol step 3 (Force exhaustion); also feeds steps 1, 4, 5
scenarios: A large ticket clears all criteria in <=20 steps → attempt 1 PASSes, leaving no failed frontier to hand off and no resume loop to run.
Attempt 1 hits a real criterion FAIL or an LLMUnavailableError, so the 'partial bank' the copy-and-seed step depends on is either a genuine-fail state or absent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to step 3: assert the attempt-1 verdict is insufficiency-only before proceeding; if it PASSes at the reduced budget, lower the budget and re-run until it fails insufficiency-only or abandon that ticket; if it fails on a genuine criterion or errors environmentally, exclude the ticket and note it (INDETERMINATE) rather than seeding downstream arms from that bank.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the exact argument-matching rule for the overlap-rate metric (e.g. normalized-path exact match for reads; verbatim-pattern exact match for greps; state how range/subset overlaps are counted) so the >=30% threshold is reproducible.
evidence: 're-search overlap rate per attempt (tool calls repeating any earlier attempt's arguments, same arm)'
're-search overlap rate reduced by >=30% relative to control'
A derived metric with no fully stated computation protocol is an E2 signal-(2) ambiguity even when the shape is clear.
findings.finding: The load-bearing 're-search overlap rate' metric — 'tool calls repeating any earlier attempt's arguments, same arm' — does not state the argument-matching semantics: exact string equality on grep patterns, path normalization, whether a read of the same file with a different range counts, or how a pattern that is a subset/superset of an earlier one is treated. The GO threshold (>=30% overlap reduction) is computed from this, so the ambiguity is decision-determining.
findings.location: Step 6 (Metrics table) and Acceptance criteria (decision rule)
scenarios: Executor A counts only exact-string argument matches; executor B normalizes paths and treats a broader grep pattern as covering a narrower one — they get materially different overlap rates and cross the 30% threshold differently.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Step 6: 'A tool call counts as re-search if its normalized arguments exactly match an earlier same-arm call — file reads keyed on absolute-normalized path (range ignored), greps keyed on verbatim pattern+dir, dir-lists on normalized dir. Overlap rate = re-search calls / total calls that attempt.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the exact equality/normalization predicate used to (a) build the searched-set frontier block and (b) count re-search overlap (e.g. normalized repo-relative paths, verbatim grep-pattern strings), and apply it identically to both arms.
evidence: Plan quote step 6: 're-search overlap rate per attempt (tool calls repeating any earlier attempt's arguments, same arm)'.
Plan quote step 4: 'derive per-criterion searched-set (paths read, patterns tried)'.
ABSENCE: no matching rule (case, path normalization, relative vs absolute, regex equivalence) for deciding when two tool-call argument sets count as the same searched item.
findings.finding: The predicate for 'repeating any earlier attempt's arguments' — which both derives the per-criterion searched-set that becomes the LLM-consumed frontier block and computes the overlap-rate metric — is unspecified (exact string match vs normalized paths/globs, and how semantically-equivalent-but-textually-different grep patterns are counted).
findings.location: Protocol steps 4 (Extract frontier) and 6 (Metrics table); Acceptance criteria (overlap-rate line)
scenarios: Two attempts read the same file via a relative vs absolute path, or grep the same code with slightly different regex → counted as overlap or not, changing both the block contents and the >=30% GO threshold outcome.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

AC item 'Harness exists in the experiment worktree (throwaway; NOT pushed to Gerrit; no s' cites operational evidence (merge_gate) that lives outside the codebase but is not tagged [operator-attested]; prefix the checkbox text with [operator-attested] so the completion verifier accepts a recorded attestation instead of failing to find code proof.
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the single reduced-budget value to use (or the rule for choosing it per ticket so attempt-1 reliably FAILs insufficiency-only) rather than an 'e.g. 12-20' range.
evidence: 'monkeypatches verify_step_floor to return the reduced budget (e.g. 12-20 steps) for every arm and attempt uniformly'
findings.finding: The reduced budget is given as a range with 'e.g.' ('the reduced budget (e.g. 12-20 steps)') rather than a single decided value. Since attempt-1 exhaustion and every arm/attempt must use it UNIFORMLY, an undecided exact value is a defaultable gap — the executor should not have to pick it fresh.
scenarios: Executor picks 12 for one ticket and 20 for another, or attempt-1 fails to actually exhaust at the chosen value on a smaller-surface ticket.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that per-arm temp cache namespaces are torn down (tempfile.TemporaryDirectory or explicit rmtree) at the end of each run so nothing accumulates.
evidence: 'the harness monkeypatches cache_dir ... to return a per-arm temp dir'
'Its populated cache is then COPIED once and each resume arm reads its own identical copy.'
No explicit teardown/cleanup of the per-arm temp dirs is described.
findings.finding: The shared-state (per-arm temp cache namespace) lifecycle covers create/update/consume but does not state a RETIRE/cleanup step for the temp cache directories after the run.
scenarios: Repeated PoC runs accumulate orphaned temp cache dirs on disk.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name and briefly contrast the external prior art the frontier-handoff hypothesis instantiates (Reflexion-style cross-trial reflection; agent scratchpad-memory that avoids re-exploring searched states), stating what the DATA-shaped exclusion-frontier variant is expected to add beyond it, so the GO/NO-GO screen and the production-telemetry recommendation rest on a stated baseline.
evidence: Plan hypothesis: 'does handing a resumption the prior attempt's search frontier as an EXCLUSION list ("already searched, found nothing: ...") measurably reduce re-search overlap and steps-to-verdict?'
Retrieved web source (letsdatascience.com, 'Building AI Agents: ReAct, Planning, and Tool Use'): 'Scratchpad memory tracks which papers have been reviewed to avoid redundant searches.'

Retrieved web source (turingpost.com, 'Reflection in AI: Reflexion, ReAct'): 'Reflexion shows the value of post-hoc reflection – after completing a trial, reflect and try again – to gradually converge on a correct solution.'

Plan grounds only the INTERNAL injection seam in prior art ('mirrors the framework's own evidence precedent', gate_ops.py:226-228 build_child_closure_evidence); no external agent-memory/reflection pattern is named.
findings.finding: The experiment's core hypothesis — handing a resumption the prior attempt's exploration trace as a 'searched-and-empty' exclusion frontier to reduce redundant re-search — is an established external agent pattern (Reflexion: post-hoc reflection carried across retry trials; and agent scratchpad-memory that tracks already-explored states to avoid redundant searches), which the plan never names or contrasts against, even though it thoroughly considers INTERNAL prior art (the framework's own build_child_closure_evidence / epic-bug-screen evidence-attachment precedent and the locust auto-resume machinery).
findings.location: Why section + Protocol step 4/5 (frontier extraction and treatment arm)
scenarios: Reviewer or operator asks what the exclusion-frontier variant adds beyond textbook Reflexion/scratchpad memory before green-lighting a real (productized) investment.
Framing the GO/NO-GO deliverable and the 'what telemetry production would need to carry' note without reference to how comparable agent-memory designs scope their trace state.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Why section, add a sentence acknowledging the hypothesis is a bounded instance of the Reflexion / agent-scratchpad-memory prior art (cite the retrieved sources), and note the distinguishing bet under test: a DATA-shaped, fence-inert, per-criterion searched-set exclusion block spliced at the framework evidence seam rather than free-form model self-reflection. Tie this framing to the 'what telemetry production would need to carry' deliverable.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that re-search overlap rate is computed over the criteria actually RE-VERIFIED in each attempt (i.e. those not yet banked in that arm's accruing cache), so the A/B denominator stays comparable and the >=30% screen is well-defined.
evidence: Step 6: 're-search overlap rate per attempt (tool calls repeating any earlier attempt's arguments, same arm)'

Step 5: 'the cache accrues within the arm across attempts (that accrual IS the resume mechanism)' — so each resume re-verifies only still-un-banked criteria, per the verdict-cache skip behavior (completion_verdict_cache.py criterion_cache_key)
Both arms share identical cache-seeding, so they remain comparable; the risk is only that an undefined denominator makes the >=30% threshold ambiguous
findings.finding: The re-search overlap metric does not define its denominator against the confound that the seeded/accrued verdict cache legitimately skips already-credited criteria on resume, shrinking the set of re-verified criteria each attempt for BOTH arms.
findings.location: Protocol step 6 (Metrics table) / AC line 'overlap rate, PASS-per-step, attempts, cost'
scenarios: A resume attempt where the cache has banked most criteria will show few re-search tool calls in BOTH arms regardless of the frontier block, deflating the overlap signal
If overlap is computed over ALL tool calls (including calls on already-banked criteria that never fire) versus only re-verified criteria, the A-vs-B comparison and the 30% screen shift
findings.suggested_fix: In step 6, define overlap rate as (tool calls in this attempt whose arguments repeat an earlier attempt in the same arm) / (tool calls issued this attempt), scoped to criteria still un-banked at attempt start — identical scoping for A and B.
